images.author: Feng Wei
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies a solitary wild kiang in Shuanghu, Tibet. Promising single-animal composition; 1024px fallback, with larger dimensions and watermark status unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Source identifies Equus kiang holdereri at Dong Gei Cuo Na Lake, Qinghai, and states its photographs show wild animals unless specified otherwise. Chestnut-and-white animals in open plateau habitat; native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Coke Smith
images.why: Another species-labelled photograph from the Qinghai gallery: a small wild herd with standing and grazing animals. Clear habitat context; group composition is less ideal for a tight 9:10 crop. Native dimensions unverified.

images.author: reurinkjan
images.why: Photographer's title and caption identify Tibetan wild ass, Equus kiang; photographed in September 2011. Species-confirmed alternative, but the 1024px file falls below the preferred resolution and watermark status is unverified.

images.author: reurinkjan
images.why: Caption confirms Equus kiang with Mount Kailash in Tibet, providing distinctive geographic context. Environmental alternative; 1024px fallback and suitability for a tight crop remain limitations.

images.author: Paul Jones
images.why: Explicit Equus kiang identification and firsthand account of wild animals on the Tibetan Plateau. Two-animal interaction; shedding coats are less polished than the desired summer appearance. 1024px fallback.

images.author: yogibaba1982
images.why: Caption and firsthand travel account identify a wild kiang galloping beside Tso Kar, Ladakh. Dynamic single-animal alternative; original dimensions and watermark status unverified.

images.author: Milo Burcham
images.why: Caption explicitly identifies Equus kiang photographed in Yeniugou, Qinghai. Full-bodied running animals against plateau mountains; strong environmental alternative, although the wide herd arrangement limits 9:10 cropping and resolution is unverified.

images.author: Michal Vaško
images.why: Caption identifies a bull elk beside a Yellowstone riverbank; source also tags Cervus canadensis. Standing animal and natural surroundings make this a strong poster candidate. Original-file URL; dimensions unverified.

images.author: Taylor Mikkelsen
images.why: Explicitly captioned as a bull elk standing in a dry grassy field at Estes Park. Promising classic standing-bull composition; 3000px rendition requested, with native dimensions unverified.

images.author: Natasha Miller
images.why: Photographer explicitly identifies this bull elk in Rocky Mountain National Park during October. Strong species and wild-location evidence; check framing before a full-body 9:10 crop. Native dimensions unverified.

images.author: NPS / Neal Herbert
images.why: Official park caption confirms a bull elk bugling at Mammoth Hot Springs. Expressive rutting behaviour and verified public-domain status; supplied 1024px fallback is below the preferred resolution.

images.author: Jim Peaco
images.why: Official caption identifies a bull elk near Yellowstone's North Entrance and Electric Peak. Useful mountain-context alternative; supplied 1024px fallback is below the preferred resolution.

images.author: NPS / Addy Falgoust
images.why: Official park photograph explicitly titled 'Bull elk during rut (1)', taken in October 2022. Species-confirmed autumn alternative; 1024px fallback, with full-body crop suitability unverified.

images.author: Alla Kemelmakher
images.why: Source identifies the animal as elk at Mammoth, Yellowstone National Park. Standing subject against a pale landscape offers separation; sex, antler prominence and native dimensions need visual confirmation.

images.author: christie greene
images.why: Photographer explicitly captions a bull elk bugling with a calf at Evergreen Lake, Colorado. Water and behaviour add interest; secondary animal and potentially obscured lower legs make this a fallback. Native dimensions unverified.
